findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None and is dereferenced on every request
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is computed for every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not set. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is Optional; it is None when the caller is not an org member, for example API-key/token auth where `request.user` is AnonymousUser, or staff accessing an org they don't belong to. For any such non-superuser caller, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises AttributeError. That turns the previously working default (DateTimePaginator) path into a 500. At minimum, only evaluate this when `use_optimized` is true and guard against `member is None`.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is incompatible with the `datetime` ordering it is used with
findings.body: The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` does `math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, 'datetime'))`. Calling `math.floor` on a `datetime.datetime` raises TypeError, so any non-empty page crashes inside `build_cursor`. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value. `build_queryset` then emits `"sentry_auditlogentry"."datetime" <= <int>`, which Postgres rejects (timestamp vs integer). The optimized path therefore fails on the first page and on every cursor-based page. It needs DateTimePaginator-style conversion, e.g. by subclassing DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django; 'advanced' path always 500s
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for negative slice bounds. So the advertised feature can never return results and turns any crafted cursor like `0:-5:0` into an unhandled 500. The comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. The comment saying this gives 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' describes an intent that should not ship. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError (as OffsetPaginator does), not passed through.

findings.title: Admin gate uses raw `is_superuser` flag and `has_global_access`, not an admin check
findings.body: The code says advanced pagination is restricted to 'authorized administrators', but the gate is `request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access`. Sentry requires an active superuser session (`is_active_superuser(request)`) for superuser privileges; checking the raw user flag bypasses that elevation step. `has_global_access` is also true for ordinary members in orgs with open membership (allow_joinleave), so it is not an admin check at all. Any privilege-gated behavior here is reachable by far more users than intended.

findings.title: BasePaginator change and comment are misleading; prev cursors with negative offsets still crash
findings.body: The new line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` only clamps negative offsets for next-cursors. A prev-cursor with a negative offset is still passed straight to `queryset[offset:stop]`, and Django raises ValueError (500). The comment says negative offsets are allowed for 'efficient bidirectional pagination' and that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions'. Neither is true, and this shared base class is used by many endpoints. Clamped negative offsets are also still fed into `build_cursor` via `cursor.offset`, producing nonsensical next/prev offsets. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError instead.

findings.title: Comment claims a behavior change that the code does not make
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed 'for advanced pagination scenarios', but `self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged and does no validation either way. The comment documents a nonexistent feature, and negative offsets are not actually usable because Django rejects negative slicing. Remove the comment, or add explicit validation that rejects negative offsets.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, a new branch in the audit log endpoint, and changes BasePaginator slicing semantics without any tests. Even a basic test requesting `?optimized_pagination=true` as a superuser with one audit log entry would fail with TypeError from `math.floor(datetime)`. A test with a non-member/API-key caller would hit the AttributeError on `member.has_global_access`.
